summary: Describes how Novell IPX works over various wide area links, specifically the IPXWAN protocol Novell uses for routers to exchange needed information before normal IPX routing traffic. It was replaced by RFC 1634.

eli5.summary: Two routers meet over a long wire and first greet each other and swap basic facts. IPXWAN is that greeting for Novell networks.

questions: how do novell routers discover each other on wan links
how does ipxwan choose routing protocols
subtitle: How Novell IPX routers establish and configure themselves across wide-area network links.

tldr.problem: Novell IPX is a connectionless datagram protocol, but wide-area network links are often connection-oriented and require initial setup before routing traffic can flow.
tldr.mechanism: IPXWAN is a protocol for IPX routers to negotiate link parameters after the WAN link is established. Routers exchange Timer Requests to determine master/slave roles and routing protocol choice, then exchange Information packets to agree on network numbers, link delays, and router names.
tldr.outcome: IPXWAN provides a common way for IPX to work consistently over many different WAN media (PPP, X.25, Frame Relay). It was later replaced by RFC 1634.

today: RFC 1551 is an Informational document that was obsoleted by RFC 1634 in August 1994, which updated the IPXWAN protocol specification.

sections.title: Novell IPX Over WAN Media
sections.content:
Novell IPX is a connectionless datagram protocol that assumes an underlying network layer (IP in the Internet world). But WAN links—whether PPP, X.25, Frame Relay, or others—are often connection-oriented, with different link establishment methods for each media type.

This RFC describes the common IPXWAN protocol that Novell uses for routers to exchange necessary information before beginning normal IPX routing and data traffic. IPXWAN is media-independent: both sides negotiate the same parameters regardless of whether the underlying link is PPP, X.25 SVC, X.25 PVC, Frame Relay, or another WAN medium.
sections.eli5: IPXWAN is a greeting that happens after a WAN link connects but before routers start sending real traffic. It is the same greeting no matter what kind of link it is.

sections.title: Negotiation and Information Exchange
sections.content:
IPXWAN operates in two main steps.

First, both sides send Timer Request packets with information about their capabilities: which routing protocols they support, whether they can assign network numbers to the WAN link, and whether they support header compression. These Timer Requests also let the routers gauge the link delay by measuring the round-trip time. The side with the larger primary network number becomes the link master, and the other becomes the slave.

Second, the master sends an Information Request packet specifying the network number to be used on the link, the calculated link delay for routing metrics, and the router's symbolic name (for network management). The slave responds with an Information Response to confirm. If the negotiated routing protocol needs workstation dial-in support, the router assigns a network number and NIC (MAC) address to the workstation.

Retries occur every 20 seconds, with a minimum timeout of 60 seconds or a maximum of 16 retries. If critical information is missing (such as an Information option), the link is disconnected.
sections.eli5: Two routers have a conversation: first they compare notes about what they can do, and one becomes the leader. Then the leader tells the other one what network number to use and how fast the link is.

sections.title: Packet Types and Routing Protocols
sections.content:
IPXWAN uses four main packet types: Timer Request (type 00), Timer Response (type 01), Information Request (type 02), and Information Response (type 03). All packets use socket number 0x9004 (a Novell-reserved socket for IPXWAN) and IPX packet type 04 (Packet Exchange).

Currently defined routing types are: Numbered RIP/SAP (type 0), NLSP (type 1), Unnumbered RIP/SAP (type 2), On-demand static routing (type 3), and Workstation routing (type 4). For backwards compatibility, routers should include type 0 if full interoperability is required. A router must not send a single Routing Type option if that type is only Workstation; it must also include one or more other routing types marked as not accepted, so workstations can detect they are connecting to a router, not another workstation.

Each packet contains a WIdentifier confidence field (hex 57415341, which is ASCII "WASM"), a sequence number, and a variable-length options list. Options carry information about routing types, extended node IDs, header compression capabilities, and padding.
sections.eli5: The IPXWAN packets are like envelopes: they tell each router what the other router can do, and they use a secret identifier so routers know they are talking to a real IPXWAN protocol, not something else.

sections.title: Network Numbers and Node Addresses
sections.content:
Every IPXWAN router has a primary network number: a unique identifier for the entire internet that persists across all links. This number is used as the WNodeID field to determine master/slave roles by comparing numbers as if each byte is an unsigned integer, with the first byte as most significant.

When the master allocates node numbers to clients or other devices, it should use the form 02:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX (where the first byte 02 indicates a non-multicast, locally administered address in IEEE address space). Node numbers of zero or all-ones (broadcast) are not allowed, and the NIC address should be incremented for each new connection to allow workstations to specify their old address on reconnect.

For WAN links using Numbered RIP protocols, the master assigns a unique common network number. For Unnumbered RIP, On-demand routing, or Workstation protocols, the common network number is zero. The link delay (in milliseconds) is calculated from the round-trip time of the Timer Request/Response exchange and is used as the transport time metric in RIP advertisements.
sections.eli5: Each router has a unique number, and the routers compare numbers to decide who is the boss. The boss then assigns network numbers to everything else on the link.

sections.title: Operation Over Different WAN Media
sections.content:
IPXWAN begins immediately after the underlying link is established, but "established" means different things for different media. Over PPP, the IPX NCP (Network Control Protocol) must reach the Open state first. Over X.25 SVCs (switched virtual circuits), the protocol identifier 0x800000008137 is used in the Call User Data field. Over X.25 PVCs (permanent virtual circuits), IPXWAN begins when Layer 2 comes up. Over Frame Relay PVCs, IPXWAN begins when the PVC transitions from inactive to active.

Either side of a connection can initiate teardown by sending a Terminate-Request on PPP or by closing the X.25 virtual circuit. When a router detects lost connectivity, it immediately reflects that in its routing database instead of waiting for timeout.

Each IPX packet is encapsulated directly in the appropriate WAN framing (X.25 or Frame Relay) without additional protocol framing. IPX network number zero is interpreted as a local network of unknown number, useful for IPXWAN packets sent before the common network number is known.
sections.eli5: Different WAN links connect differently: some need a handshake, some are always on, some have virtual circuits. IPXWAN works the same way no matter which one you use.
